tagline: Bluff by bluff along the strait, out to Neah Bay.
intro: West of Port Angeles, SR 112 crosses the Elwha River gorge on a deck arch bridge and follows an old railroad grade across a rural plain to Joyce. Past Twin Beach it takes to the coastal bluffs, with a hairpin at every creek, comes down to the shore at Pysht, then swings inland and back out to the twin villages of Clallam Bay and Sekiu. The last miles keep to the strait, Vancouver Island across the water.

The road was a wagon road in the 1920s and reached Neah Bay in 1953. A plan to carry it on down the ocean coast drew a 22-mile protest hike in 1958, Justice William O. Douglas among the walkers. It was never built.

moments.title: Salt Creek Recreation Area
moments.text: A wartime Army fort on the strait, the casemates of its 16-inch guns still standing, now keeps campsites, trails and the tidepools at Tongue Point.

moments.title: Clallam Bay
moments.text: A steamboat stop of the 1880s at the mouth of the Clallam River, where the Slip Point light was first lit on April Fool's Day, 1905.

moments.title: Makah Museum, Neah Bay
moments.text: At the end of the road the Makah show artifacts from Ozette, a village of theirs partly buried by a mudslide around 1750, along with canoes, basketry and whaling gear.

practical: A Makah Recreation Permit must be displayed in your vehicle for outdoor activities on reservation land around Neah Bay.
